cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: The Logic Gets Bigger
cards.instruction: Use every new detail to expand the impossible system, its history, and the consequences of breaking it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Our meeting chairs float at noon. Book the ceiling; they've had landing rights since the first furniture strike.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't we stand and tie the chairs down?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Restraint broke the last treaty. That's when the desks joined them. We'll need an airspace permit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The caretaker only issues floor permits.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then promote her to altitude minister before the cabinets claim the roof.

mechanism: A assumes jurisdiction over an impossible negotiation and uses each report to enlarge its history, political rules and consequences before deciding B next action.
confusable: D162 invents a local rule as needed; D168 must also expand system history and consequences, with A directing the response as the highest authority.
comparison: Office furniture territory extends labor history into permits; dinner crockery expands greeting into trade and borders.
seedUse: Both Stance and both Drive seeds read. Preserve the furniture treaty and crockery diplomacy histories where already causal; retain strong fusion rather than force a new institution or prop.
